character: Compact 3.9km British circuit with dramatic elevation changes, blind crests, and the iconic Paddock Hill Bend. Natural amphitheatre setting. Technical and flowing, demanding precision on bumpy surfaces.

corners.name: Paddock Hill Bend
corners.technique: Brake after the 'two' board while slightly turning in. Blind apex — the corner drops away steeply. Late apex, let car drift to exit
corners.trap: Braking too late into the blind downhill; understeer into the gravel

corners.name: Druids
corners.technique: Hard braking uphill, 1st or 2nd gear. Late apex, progressive throttle on exit
corners.trap: Locking fronts on the uphill approach; early apex kills exit speed down Graham Hill

corners.name: Graham Hill Bend
corners.technique: Brake before outside kerbing starts, 2nd gear, mid-point apex. Don't cut inside kerb (causes TC/spin)
corners.trap: Too much inside kerb causes instability on the bumpy downhill

corners.name: Surtees
corners.technique: Tricky off-camber corner — brake at the 'one' board, trail brake in. Good exit feeds long straight to Hawthorn
corners.trap: Off-camber catches out — understeer on entry is common; need good car rotation

corners.name: Hawthorn Bend
corners.technique: Brake before 'one' board, 3rd-4th gear, trail brake to inside kerb. Turn in early, hug inside, get on throttle ASAP
corners.trap: Not committing to the speed — hesitation here costs hugely

corners.name: Westfield Bend
corners.technique: Brake at 'one' board, 3rd gear, trail brake in. Cut inside kerb, use all exit kerb and matting
corners.trap: Not using enough kerb — track limits are lenient here, exploit them

corners.name: Sheene Curve
corners.technique: Smooth direction changes at speed, carry momentum through both parts
corners.trap: Over-driving causes snap on direction change

corners.name: Clark Curve
corners.type: fast left leading to Paddock Hill (T9)
corners.technique: Clean exit onto start/finish straight — exit speed is critical
corners.trap: Running wide loses speed all the way down the pit straight
